column1: # RECIPE_MEMORY.tsv - append-only lesson memory of recipe scoped-leases-20261106 (RELOCATE_SCOPED_LEASES): one row per lesson, appended in the same commit as the correction.

column4: a donor type that lives in the donor package but is owned elsewhere in M3JDK (M3RuntimeHeap -> jdk.m3.util.M3RuntimeHeap) is a DEPENDENCY row: the recipe adds one import after the last import of every Java file whose code lines name it, and nothing for comment-only mentions (M3ByteSlices/M3CompositeBytes -> jdk.internal.m3 appear only in the Javadoc of M3JniByteConcat), so no --add-exports java.base/jdk.internal.m3 and no --patch-module is needed
column5: M3ScopedLeaseTable.java differs from the donor by the header, the package line, the anchor and one import line; M3JniByteConcat compiles with no jdk.internal.m3 import; first mvn run compiled 7 main sources on the module path

column4: a donor package name inside a text block or string literal is not an import line: the code-carrier oracle compiles "import <donor package>.M3NativeLeaseScan;" in memory at run time, so the PACKAGE rows apply as a word-bounded dotted literal to every body line (before the JNI and TEXT rows); body_match_renamed stays TRUE because the same declared rows are applied to the donor body
column5: diff of M3NativeLeaseCodeCarrierOracle.java: line 48 of the BRIDGE text block renamed; native matrix M3_LEASE_CODE_CARRIER_PASS permutations=6 for the relocated family

column4: a static import (import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*) resolves through the package of its class, not through the class as a package: map_import takes the static flag and looks the class's package up in the PACKAGE/EXTERNAL rows (the sibling lanes' lesson "static imports need their own map rule" is absorbed into the recipe instead of adding one EXTERNAL row per class)
column5: M3NativeLeaseFullscanContractTest, M3JniByteConcatTest, M3JniArrayReferencesTest carry static imports; relocate.py: 0 refusals with the single EXTERNAL row org.junit.jupiter.api

column4: C and CMake files have no package line and other header styles: the donor header (// lines, # lines, one /* */ block of Copyright/SPDX lines, or a /* SPDX */ one-liner) is replaced by the M3JDK header in the file's own comment style, the anchor goes right after the header (//FLLDCIM: in C, #FLLDCIM: in CMake), JNI rows rewrite the exported symbols and the javac -h header names, TEXT rows the CMake paths; body_match is FALSE and body_match_renamed TRUE for them by construction
column5: PROVENANCE.tsv: m3_scoped_leases.c and scoped-leases/CMakeLists.txt FALSE/TRUE; cc -Wpedantic accepts the // anchor in C17; cmake configure+build of the relocated subproject PASS

column4: what jdk_naming.py would rewrite afterwards is declared as a TEXT row instead, so the recipe output is already the naming fixed point and relocate --check stays at changed=0 after jdk_naming apply: the system property synexia.test.requireNative -> jdk.m3.jni.requireNative (module-package prefix, JDK property style; the SEGMENT_DOT rule would have produced m3.test.requireNative) and the prose product name M3JDK21 -> M3JDK 21 (PROSE_PRODUCT_VERSION)

column4: javac -Xlint:missing-explicit-ctor fires for a public class without an explicit constructor in an exported package of a named module (M3ScopedLeaseTable); the donor compiled on the classpath where the lint is silent; the body stays the donor's, the lint is off for the module with a comment, and the explicit constructor belongs to the donor's next revision (fix the donor, re-run the recipe), never to a hand edit of the relocated file
column5: first mvn run: BUILD FAILURE "class jdk.m3.jni.M3ScopedLeaseTable in exported package jdk.m3.jni declares no explicit constructors"; second run with -Xlint:all,-requires-automatic,-missing-explicit-ctor: BUILD SUCCESS

column4: the M3RuntimeHeap owner artifact (m3/ports/collections, m3-collection-port-wave1) has no module descriptor: module-info requires its automatic module name m3.collection.port.wave1, the requires-automatic lint is off, maven-compiler warns "Required filename-based automodules detected" (a warning, not an error); the tests compile and run on the classpath (useModulePath=false on default-testCompile and surefire) because the code-carrier oracle uses javax.tools, which the module does not require
column5: jar --describe-module: requires m3.collection.port.wave1; mvn log WARNING automodules; Tests run: 25

column4: a Maven coordinate written as text in a Java comment (groupId:artifactId) is renamed by the PKG_COM_M3 rule because the GROUP_ID keep-span covers only the <groupId> XML element: comments name the artifact and the directory, never the groupId literal

column4: a new default module whose dependency is an m3 sibling must bring that sibling into the reactor: <module>native</module> alone broke a full mvn -f make/m3/pom.xml (com.m3.compat:m3-collection-port-wave1 unresolved outside the reactor, found by the lane owner on PR #2513); revision b (branch m3/native-scoped-leases-20261106b) adds <module>ports/collections</module> before it (the reactor orders by dependency anyway); ports/collections can be a reactor module because its vendored JUnit 5.10.2-m3-source-1 is the same vendored family six default modules already require; the reactor parse needs every module pom, so the sparse tree takes /m3/**/pom.xml
